title: Dicts
explain: A dictionary maps keys to values and looks them up quickly. You read with `d[key]`, or `d.get(key, default)` when the key might be missing. Loop over `d.items()` to get keys and values together.
code:
scores = {"Ada": 91, "Linus": 78}
scores["Grace"] = 85
print(scores["Ada"])
print(scores.get("Alan", 0))      # 0, no error
for name, score in scores.items():
    print(name, score)
print("Linus" in scores)          # True
del scores["Linus"]
print(len(scores))
exercise: Count how many times each letter appears in a word and print the result as a dictionary.
tip: Reading a missing key with `d[key]` raises `KeyError`. Use `d.get(key)` or check `key in d` first.
